question: A cloud droplet is 0.02 mm across; a small raindrop is 1 mm. How many droplets make one raindrop, in thousands?
move: When size grows in every direction at once, multiply the growth three times.
trap: Answering 50, as if droplets lined up end to end.
hint: Droplets merge by volume; compare the widths first.
steps: Volume goes with the cube of width: 50 x 50 x 50.
reference: Pruppacher & Klett, Microphysics of Clouds and Precipitation, Kluwer, 1997
